decisions.decision: Use the current canonical inventory /a e i o u p b t d k g m n f v s z l r j w/: five vowels and sixteen consonants/glides. The official letters are a e i o u p b t d k g m n f v s z l r j w.

Do not include independent /ʃ h ŋ ə ɲ/ phonemes. Schwa is absent from the canonical inventory and alphabet. [ʃ], [ŋ], and [ɲ] may arise only through the separately defined coalescent or assimilatory realizations of canonical sequences/morphophonemes; /h/ has no canonical letter or phoneme.
Use lexical /a e i o u/. Use /a i u/ for the grammar-critical person subsystem; /e o/ remain lexical vowels and optional referential-specificity markers.
Retain canonical /j/ and /w/, written j and w. The letter j always represents the palatal glide /j/ and never the affricate /dʒ/; w always represents /w/.
Use one rhotic category /r/ with broad acceptable rhotic realizations; do not prescribe trill, tap, approximant, or uvular realization.

Retain /b d ɡ v z/ as canonical lexical contrasts for international-root recognizability, while allowing the documented accent-tolerant mergers where unambiguous. Do not rely on these fragile merger contrasts for critical grammar or protected minimal pairs.

Do not assign independent phoneme status to /ts tʃ dʒ/. Represent [ts] from /t+s/; allow /t+j/ to surface as [tj ~ tʃ] and /d+j/ as [dj ~ dʒ]. The transparent sequence pronunciation remains valid, and none of these coalescences may carry grammar-critical contrasts.

Canonical sj is the transparent sequence /s+j/. Speakers may realize it as [sj] or coalescent [ʃ] where the sequence remains recoverable and no grammar-critical contrast depends on the difference. Independent /ʃ/ remains excluded.
Do not add independent /ɲ/. Canonical gn is the transparent sequence /g+n/; [ɲ] is an accepted coalescent realization where the sequence remains recoverable and no protected contrast is lost.

The letter c is not part of the official Unisermo alphabet and has no automatic pronunciation. A source-form Latin/international c is adapted root by root to k, s, j, or tj according to international recognizability, population accessibility, genealogical dispersion, phonotactic simplicity, and lexical distinctness. Once selected, the Unisermo root spelling is fixed.

A source /dʒ/ is not mapped mechanically. Root by root it may be represented as dj (/d+j/, with [dj ~ dʒ]), j (/j/), g (/g/), z (/z/), or an etymological/international form that avoids /dʒ/, whichever best balances recognizability, accessibility, genealogical dispersion, phonotactics, and lexical distinctness. This is a recurrent root-construction procedure for divergent Romance/international outcomes, not an exceptional pronunciation rule. The letter j itself always remains /j/.

Use i/u/a for first/second/third person. Mark plural with a nasal morphophoneme /N/ written n after the person vowel: i, u, a; in, un, an. In neutral forms /N/ is normally word-final; it may be medial specifically before the optional referential-specificity suffixes -o/-e, yielding forms such as ano/ane. Default [n]; accent-tolerant place realizations [n ~ ɳ ~ m ~ ŋ ~ ɴ] are non-contrastive and may not be deleted.

Keep grammatical gender neutral by default with zero marking. Optionally mark masculine/male-specific reference with -o and feminine/female-specific reference with -e; these are semantic/referential specificity markers, not grammatical gender classes, and never trigger obligatory agreement. The neutral form always remains valid. Third person is a/ao/ae in the singular and an/ano/ane in the plural, with morphological order person + plural N + optional specificity marker. Accent-tolerant realizations may raise canonical -e toward [i] and -o toward [u] where mid vowels are unstable, but the front/back distinction must remain recoverable and the two markers may not collapse when the distinction is intended; otherwise use the neutral form or lexical paraphrase.
